effects.prompt: Destroy Cutting Couriers? If you do, this attack gets go again.

_comment:
'When your sword attack hits, you may destroy this. If you do, the attack gets go again.' Warrior Equipment - Legs.

DELIVERY: TRIGGERED + ON_HIT on the equipment itself. The engine broadcasts ON_HIT to the ATTACKER's permanent zones INCLUDING player.legs (engine.py:1437-1459, _dsl_permanent_zones), so the legs slot hears its controller's own attacks - no delivery-side scoping needed. The two conditions ARE the printed gate ('YOUR SWORD attack'), evaluated at resolution while state.combat is live: ATTACK_SUBTYPE_IN reads 'subtypes' and unions the attack card's types AND subtypes (condition_types.py:296-316), so a Sword weapon attack matches; ATTACKER_CONTROLLED_BY_YOU (condition_types.py:389-396) compares combat.attack_card.controller to the equipment's controller.

MAY = the printed 'you may destroy this. If you do, ...': declining runs NOTHING in the block - no destroy, no go again (handler effect_types.py:3788-3856 reads prompt/effects; sub-effects run only on accept). Release note ('if you cannot destroy, the rest is not generated') is satisfied structurally: the destroy COST-style can_pay is not involved here, and while the equipment is in play destroying it is always possible, so the option is always offered.

ORDER inside the block follows the sentence: DESTROY_SELF (effect_types.py:2470 shares the DESTROY_PERMANENT branch; canonical destroy() resolves the equipment-slot zone) THEN GO_AGAIN. Destroying first cannot strand the grant: _grant_go_again (effect_types.py:423-458) needs only state.combat in the combat path, not the card's zone. During ON_HIT combat exists, so CR 8.3.5b applies - 'Go Again' lands on state.combat.keywords (dedup-guarded per 8.3.5c) and the engine pays the action point at the Resolution Step. That IS 'the attack gets go again': the point arrives because this attack carried the keyword.

PRINTED KEYWORD DELIBERATELY NOT AUTHORED AND NOT STRIPPED: GoAgain appears in printed_keywords, but it is the DB flattening the bolded words inside the triggered sentence - the card itself never has go again under any reading (the ATTACK does). loader.conditional_keywords (loader.py:255-296) strips a printed keyword only from an ability gated on SOURCE_IS_ATTACK granting it to ITSELF; this grant targets the attack, which is exactly the Luminaris case that docstring says must NOT strip. Residual exposure is nil in practice: a GoAgain keyword sitting on legs equipment is inert (equipment is never played and never becomes combat.attack_card).

No gaps; every clause expressible.
